It shares a lot of similarities with the 'aloof professor' trope (which is actually reasonably common), and also demonstrates the problem with trying to communicate large amounts of information at once. When you find something interesting or amiss, it becomes an adventure of sorts while you sniff out the various clues trying to piece the big picture together. Whether academic or conspiratorial, it tends to be all-consuming until you reach your solution, and you forget many common-sense things about life. Additionally, when you have a large amount of information to convey, you generally have to get the pre-reqs (read: uninteresting info) out of the way so the interesting info makes sense. When under pressure, you tend to jump right to the big message, which is lost on the crowd (since no pre-reqs), and you appear literally crazy.

It's actually why, instead of massive diatribes, I only leave small self-contained notes on topics, always with the offer to provide more info / invitation to ask questions (which, believe it or not, people have actually taken me up on).
